claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is driven by reversible magnetoelastic coupling.
Small compositional changes induce local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions modulate magnetic exchange interactions.
Modulation of magnetic exchange enables magnetic moments to reorient under low applied fields.
The proposed magnetoelastic response preserves rapid heat transport.
The proposed magnetoelastic response produces minimal magnetic or thermal hysteresis.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous high-entropy matrix with minimal pre-existing strain.
The initial alloy has minimal phase separation.
Substitution by an element of similar atomic size but different valence-electron count can controllably induce nanoscale lattice distortions.
Induced lattice distortions enhance magnetoelastic coupling.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling facilitates rapid, low-hysteresis magnetic-moment reordering under low applied fields.
Rapid magnetic-moment reordering boosts the magnetocaloric effect.
The modified alloy will have a larger low-field isothermal entropy change than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have a larger low-field adiabatic temperature change than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have lower thermal hysteresis than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will maintain a high heat-exchange rate relative to the baseline.
The mechanism will maintain structural properties despite compositionally induced lattice distortion.
The hypothesis applies while the alloy retains a single-phase high-entropy microstructure and is operated near its magnetic transition under fields below 1 T.
High fields or multiphase structures may not exhibit the predicted behavior.
The interplay between lattice distortion and magnetic exchange is supported in similar magnetocaloric materials.
